- Students must consult with the course instructor informally within 14 days of official grade release if they question their final grade.
- If the informal consultation is unresolved, a formal Grade Appeal Form must be submitted to the Department Chair within 30 days.
- The departmental review committee must provide a final binding ruling within 21 business days of receiving the appeal.

- Course instructors must provide accessible course materials and syllabus formats upon request, in compliance with ADA Section 508.
- Instructors must acknowledge accommodation letters from the Disability Resource Center within 3 business days of receiving them.
- Disputes about reasonable accommodations should be escalated directly to the University ADA Coordinator for final resolution.

- Unauthorized sharing of institutional credentials, bypassing network firewalls, or hosting unapproved external servers on the campus subnet leads to a 72-hour account suspension pending a security review.
- Permanent revocation of access requires formal clearance from the Chief Information Security Officer.
- These actions are strictly prohibited and can result in immediate account suspension.

Here is a summary of the university policy in three concise bullet points:

• Faculty must provide accessible course materials and syllabus formats upon request from students with disabilities.
• If a student with a disability requests an accommodation letter from the Disability Resource Center, the course instructor must acknowledge receipt of the letter within 3 business days.
• Disputes regarding reasonable accommodations are resolved directly with the University ADA Coordinator, who makes binding decisions.

Here is a summary of the university policy in three concise bullet points:

• To access university computing resources, you must have active institutional credentials.
• If you share your credentials with others, bypass network firewalls, or host unapproved external servers on the campus subnet, your account will be suspended for 72 hours.
• If your account is suspended, you can request a security review to have your account reinstated, but permanent revocation is possible if you do not receive formal clearance from the Chief Information Security Officer.

- Suspected academic integrity violations must be reported to the Academic Honor Board within 7 calendar days of discovery.
- First-time offenders receive a zero ('0%') on the assignment.
- Students can appeal a written sanction to the Provost Office within 10 business days.
- Repeat offenders face a minimum penalty of one academic term suspension.

Here is a summary of the university policy in three concise bullet points:

• If you disagree with your semester final grade, you must talk to your instructor within 14 calendar days of when the grade is officially released.
• If you're still unhappy with the grade after talking to your instructor, you must submit a formal Grade Appeal Form to the Department Chair within 30 calendar days.
• The Department Chair's review committee will make a final decision on your appeal within 21 business days of receiving your appeal.

- Directory information can be disclosed without consent until a formal nondisclosure request is filed within the first 10 calendar days of the academic term.
- Educational records, grades, and advisor notes are strictly confidential and cannot be shared with unvetted third-party cloud applications or external entities without a institutional data-use agreement.
- There are no exceptions to these confidentiality rules; all university staff must adhere to these guidelines.

Here is a summary of the university policy in three concise bullet points:

• Within the first 10 calendar days of each academic term, you must submit a formal nondisclosure request to the university if you do not want your directory information (e.g., name, address, phone number) to be disclosed without your consent.
• University staff are required to keep all educational records, grades, and advisor notes confidential and cannot share them with unvetted third-party cloud applications or external entities without a valid institutional data-use agreement.
• There is no specific deadline for submitting a formal nondisclosure request, but it is recommended to do so within the first 10 calendar days of each term to ensure your directory information is not disclosed.

- Regular class attendance is mandatory.
- Excused absences must be notified to the instructor via email at least 24 hours in advance or within 48 hours after an unforeseen emergency.
- Unexcused absences exceeding 20% of scheduled class sessions will result in an administrative withdrawal or an automatic final grade of 'FA'. Students can contest an 'FA' grade by filing a formal written petition with the Dean of Students within 5 business days after grades are posted.

Here is a summary of the policy in three concise bullet points:

• If you suspect someone of academic integrity violation (plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, or using illicit exam aids), you must report it to the Academic Honor Board within 7 calendar days.
• If found guilty, the student will receive a zero ('0%') on the assignment, and they have 10 business days to submit an appeal to the Provost Office.
• Repeat offenses can result in a minimum suspension penalty of 1 academic term.

Here is a summary of the university policy in three concise bullet points:

• To receive an excused absence, notify your instructor via email at least 24 hours before the scheduled class or within 48 hours of an unforeseen emergency.
• Unexcused absences exceeding 20% of scheduled class sessions will result in an administrative withdrawal or an automatic final grade of 'FA'.
• To contest an 'FA' notation, submit a formal written petition to the Dean of Students within 5 business days following grade posting.
